question.worked_solution:
We can apply the distributive law

$$
AB+AC=A(B+C).
$$

So, we calculate $B+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B+C & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & \sqrt{3}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+AC & =A(B+C) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
